**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
<!--
- Frontend -> Developer tools -> Info
- Or use this command: hass --version
-->
0.102.1

**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**
Not known

**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**
<!--
Please provide details about your environment.
-->
Docker - `homeassistant/home-assistant:latest`

**Integration:**
<!--
Please add the link to the documentation at https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/ of the integration in question.
-->
[Workday (binary sensor)](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/workday/)


**Description of problem:**
According to the [docs of version 0.9.11 of `python-holidays`](https://github.com/dr-prodigy/python-holidays#available-countries), Estonia is in the list of supported countries. Despite this, the string `EE` fails configuration validation.


**Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` entries and (fill out even if it seems unimportant):**
```yaml
binary_sensor:
  - platform: workday
    country: EE
```

**Traceback (if applicable):**
```
Invalid config for [binary_sensor.workday]: value is not allowed for dictionary value @ data['country']. Got 'EE'. (See ?, line ?). Please check the docs at https://home-assistant.io/integrations/workday/
```

**Additional information:**
comments: Looks like that I didn't got all new entries with the last update.

review_comments: `Polish` is still valid but deprecated. This change would break existing setups. Thus this change would make the PR a "Breaking change".
Sorry did not know that, wil add it back :)

Oh I am sorry but it was not in the [list](url) and before removing it I tested it with `HUD` and got the following error:
```log
line 163, in setup_platform
    obj_holidays = getattr(holidays, country)(years=year)
AttributeError: module 'holidays' has no attribute 'HUD'
```
Interestingly enough after testing it again now 'HUD' does not work but `Honduras` does. Looking at your PR `Honduras` is mentioned but 'HUD' is not. Therefore, I am pretty sure `HUD` has been removed.
It's `HND` not `HUD` according the source code.
You are correct, did not see [that line](https://github.com/dr-prodigy/python-holidays/blob/a331982e9aef1580ac78883dcb21b0ce2ac6036e/holidays.py#L4011).
